summary: Customer C11663 reported unauthorized activity on card C11663-K1, referencing transaction 3660153. Investigation revealed a series of seven unauthorized online product-C transactions between January 22 and January 31, 2017, totaling $8,551.47 and escalating to four identical charges of $1,800.00. The legitimate cardholder conducted concurrent in-person purchases in regions 327 and 315, confirming the physical card remained in their possession while card credentials were breached. Furthermore, 20 other cards across distinct accounts exhibited identical batch transaction activity with sequential transaction IDs during the same period. The activity was confirmed as card-not-present fraud, and card blocking and regulatory reporting were executed.
open_question: While card-not-present fraud is established by the concurrent in-person cardholder activity and sequential cross-card batch processing, the exact point of compromise (e.g. online merchant database breach vs payment gateway compromise) remains unconfirmed. Merchant descriptor details and acquirer IP logs across the 20 peer cards would pinpoint the breach source.

waiting.why: R2: customer states they did not make the transaction; exposure $8,551.47
3a: the fraud connects to 20 other card(s), which is a connection to another customer's fraud
